title: Seat a heatsink on a processor straight down, without sliding it across the paste
instruction: Place the aluminium heatsink on the processor inside the four posts. Lower it straight down and do not slide it once it touches.
context: Server and GPU board assembly in data-centre build-out, part of the physical work of adding AI compute: a heatsink is lowered vertically onto freshly applied thermal paste. Sliding or twisting it across the die once it touches smears the paste and leaves voids that overheat the chip, and a heatsink dropped onto a bare die can chip it, so assemblers align it in the air, then set it down slowly and straight.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Circuit board: a green rigid glass-epoxy circuit board, 200 x 160 x 4 mm (200 mm along x), fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0. (2) Processor: a dark grey rigid block standing in for the processor die, 30 x 30 mm and 3 mm tall, fixed at the centre of the board's top, sides parallel to x and y; its top is 7 mm above the table. (3) Four retention posts: black rigid round pins (standoffs), 8 mm across and 14 mm tall, fixed upright on the board's top at x 26.6 and 33.4 cm, y -3.4 and +3.4 cm (the corners of a 68 mm square centred on the processor). Each stands just outside a corner of a centred heatsink, 2 mm beyond the line of its sides in x and in y and 4.5 mm from its corner, so a heatsink off along x or y alone never meets a post and one off diagonally by more than about 4.5 mm does. (4) Heatsink: a hollow aluminium block standing in for a heatsink, 56 x 56 mm and 32 mm tall, 200 g (a solid aluminium block this size would weigh 270 g), with flat faces; its top and bottom 56 x 56 mm faces are alike. It stands on the table centred at x 22.0 cm, y +22.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial. 'Touching' means the heatsink's lowest point is within 2 mm of the processor's top (above or below it) while the heatsink's outline seen from above overlaps the processor. 'Smear' is how far the heatsink slides over the processor while touching: its centre's horizontal travel plus any turn about the vertical counted at the processor's corners (21 mm times the angle in radians), over every control step that begins or ends touching. It is followed in steps of 0.2 mm: a move counts once the heatsink is 0.2 mm from where smear was last counted, so a shiver that stays within 0.2 mm adds nothing, and any remainder counts when it stops touching. 'Set-down speed' is the heatsink's fastest downward speed each time it comes down onto the processor (every approach counts, not only the first): while it is over the processor less than 10 mm above the touching height, and on the control step on which it comes to touch (including how far it came down in that step). 'Tilted' is the angle between the vertical and the axis through the heatsink's two 56 x 56 mm faces (either face may be down). 'Flat on the processor' means touching and tilted less than 2 degrees; 'centred within' is the horizontal distance between the heatsink's centre and the processor's; 'square within' is how far its sides are turned from the board's edges. Score 0 if at the end the heatsink's centre is not over the board, it is tilted more than 30 degrees, or it rests on a post (part of a post's top lies under its underside, which is at most 2 mm above that top). Otherwise: 1.0 if it is flat on the processor, centred within 2 mm and square within 3 degrees, the smear was 1 mm or less and the set-down speed 0.10 m/s or less, all held still for 2.5 s; 0.75 if it is flat on the processor, centred within 2 mm and square within 3 degrees with a smear of 5 mm or less, but the smear was over 1 mm or the set-down speed over 0.10 m/s; 0.5 if it is flat on the processor, centred within 5 mm and square within 10 degrees, whatever the smear and speed; 0.25 if it is touching the processor but not meeting 0.5 (tilted, or further off); 0 in every other case (not placed, still held above the processor, left on the board beside it). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. In a real trial, a slide or twist shows in the paste print on the die when the heatsink is lifted off, and the set-down speed is read from the video's last frames before contact against the posts' 14 mm height.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The board, processor and posts are fixed; the heatsink is a plain uniform box of the stated size and mass (no fins, screws or springs), and the posts only mark the mounting position. Thermal paste is not simulated: smear is scored from the heatsink's motion while it is within 2 mm of the processor's top. The scorer sees only the heatsink, not the gripper, so a heatsink held still within 2 mm of the processor counts as set down.
reset_notes: Put the heatsink back on the table centred at x 22.0 cm, y +22.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. Nothing is consumed (a real build wipes the die and applies fresh paste before each trial).
